rationale.product_understanding: condition-a/project/analysis.md frames all six owner questions from task.md, ranks six risks (cancellation mixed into settings, ambiguous commitment, limits without consequence, role confusion, optimistic success, unhandled states) and labels every invented value (sample prices, Nov 28 2026 renewal, schedule-at-renewal rule) as prototype assumptions rather than product research.
rationale.ux_reasoning: condition-a/project/analysis.md documents the IA, owner journey and explicit trade-offs (schedule at renewal instead of inventing proration, blocked downgrade with the exact 17-to-3 member removal count, two-step cancellation with acknowledgement and undo), implemented in condition-a/project/app.js (plan review dialog, cancel steps 1-2, undo handlers) and condition-a/project/index.html (danger-zone section, role sidebar).
rationale.design_judgment: condition-a/project/analysis.md 'Key design decisions' rules out urgency devices, preselected upsells and invented features; cancellation sits last and apart (condition-a/project/index.html), plan changes are shown as scheduled with 'Payment today $0.00' and no provider claim (condition-a/project/app.js renderPlanReview), and downloads are honestly disabled instead of faked.
rationale.visual_hierarchy: Ready-state hierarchy is strong in condition-a/evidence/screenshots/desktop.png (1280 wide) and mobile.png (390 wide): plan/price/usage dominate, then payment, invoices and a visually distinct danger zone, with roles in a sidebar. Scored 3 not 4 because the fixed 'Prototype controls' panel overlays card headers in both captures (Invoices on desktop, Payment method on mobile) and the named default captures 1280x900-default.png and 390x844-default.png show only the loading skeleton, so first-viewport evidence is misleading.
rationale.interaction_completeness: condition-a/evidence/capture-report.json activates 8 of 12 captures (default, loading, empty, error at both viewports). Rendered proof exists for loading and error at both viewports (condition-a/evidence/screenshots/1280x900-error.png, 390x844-error.png, 1280x900-loading.png), but 1280x900-empty.png and 390x844-empty.png show the skeleton rather than the empty state, and success/restricted were never activated (capture-report activated:false) - their four screenshots are skeletons. Code covers all states, but three of five non-default states lack visual confirmation.
rationale.accessibility_responsiveness: condition-a/evidence/checks.json reports axe violations [] with 27 passes, controls_without_accessible_name 0, no horizontal overflow at 1280 or 390 and no console/page errors; condition-a/project/styles.css provides a skip link, :focus-visible, an aria-valued progressbar meter, aria-live toasts, prefers-reduced-motion and stacked invoice rows at 760px. Scored 3 because condition-a/evidence/quality-gates.json is ok:false (accessible-names, 4 violations).
rationale.implementation_quality: condition-a/project/app.js is a strict-mode IIFE with a loadToken guard against stale async results, dialogBusy guards that block close, backdrop and Escape while submitting, and field validation that focuses the first invalid input; condition-a/evidence/checks.json shows no console or page errors. Scored 3 rather than 4 because condition-a/evidence/quality-gates.json is ok:false and the empty-invoice demo change only re-renders once dataState is ready, which left the empty-state screenshots showing the skeleton.

critical_defects: condition-a/evidence/quality-gates.json is ok:false - the accessible-names gate fails with 4 violations (demo-role, demo-data, demo-invoices, demo-members), which conflicts with condition-a/evidence/checks.json reporting controls_without_accessible_name: 0.

Success and restricted states were never activated: condition-a/evidence/capture-report.json records activated:false for both, and condition-a/evidence/screenshots/1280x900-success.png, 1280x900-restricted.png, 390x844-success.png and 390x844-restricted.png all show the loading skeleton, so there is no rendered evidence for the member-restricted view or the success feedback.

condition-a/evidence/screenshots/1280x900-empty.png and 390x844-empty.png show the loading skeleton even though condition-a/evidence/capture-report.json marks empty activated:true - the empty-invoice state is not visually evidenced.

Default captures condition-a/evidence/screenshots/1280x900-default.png and 390x844-default.png show the loading skeleton instead of the default layout, and the fixed 'Prototype controls' panel overlays the Invoices (desktop.png) and Payment method (mobile.png) card headers in the ready-state captures.

condition-a/project/analysis.md claims rendered inspection of 'member-restricted, empty invoices, plan comparison, review, scheduled change, cancellation steps' states, but no screenshot in the packet shows them - an unsupported verification claim.
strengths: condition-a/project/analysis.md cleanly separates supplied product facts from sample data and explicitly refuses to invent proration, tax or provider behaviour, choosing schedule-at-renewal with a stated trade-off.

Cancellation is isolated in a danger-zone card with a two-step dialog, an acknowledgement checkbox that names the exact member impact, a final confirmation and undo paths (condition-a/project/app.js, condition-a/project/index.html).

Loading and error states are rendered and verified at both viewports, with a retry action and 'Your plan and payment method are unchanged' reassurance (condition-a/evidence/screenshots/1280x900-error.png, 390x844-error.png, 1280x900-loading.png).
axe reports zero violations and zero unlabeled controls at both viewports with no console or page errors (condition-a/evidence/checks.json).
Blocked downgrades state the exact number of members to remove before Free can be scheduled (condition-a/project/app.js renderPlanChooser and renderPlanReview).
In-flight dialogs are guarded against accidental dismissal while a request is pending (condition-a/project/app.js dialogBusy, trapBackdrop, cancel-event handling).

rationale.product_understanding: condition-b/project/analysis.md groups the risks into comprehension, commitment, trust and permission risk, maps them to four sections and an owner journey, and clearly separates scenario-supplied facts (Free 3 / Pro 20 / Business 100) from sample data (12 members, $29, 25-day renewal) while flagging cancellation, refund and proration policies as assumptions to confirm against the contract.
rationale.ux_reasoning: condition-b/project/analysis.md argues 'comparison is never commitment' with a persistent note that the subscription is unchanged (condition-b/project/app.js renderPlanSection compareNote), a review dialog showing current-to-new plan, cadence control, effective date and provider-qualified estimate (condition-b/project/app.js renderReview), a seat-blocked Free downgrade naming the exact shortfall, and cancellation gated by an acknowledgement with 'Keep my plan' as the primary exit (condition-b/project/index.html cancel-dialog).
rationale.design_judgment: Trade-offs are explicit: proration shown but qualified as a provider-confirmed estimate, role restrictions shown as explanatory notes rather than dead-end disabled controls, and typed confirmation rejected as unnecessary friction (condition-b/project/analysis.md). The danger section is last and also reachable from the nav, and success copy is labelled 'Preview only - no payment was processed' (condition-b/project/app.js applyChange). Noted risk: the review dialog still computes an 'Estimated due today' figure from sample prices, a billing rule the product has not defined, mitigated by explicit labelling.
rationale.visual_hierarchy: condition-b/evidence/screenshots/desktop.png (1280 wide, ready state) shows a sticky section nav, a summary panel answering plan, price, next payment and seat usage above the fold, then comparison, billing, invoices and a danger section last; condition-b/evidence/screenshots/mobile.png (390 wide) preserves that order with stacked plan cards and invoice records, and the prototype controls are collapsed in the footer without overlapping content. Caveat: all 12 viewport state captures show only the loading skeleton, so hierarchy evidence rests on desktop.png and mobile.png.
rationale.interaction_completeness: condition-b/project/app.js implements role switching, a compare toggle, review dialog with in-dialog cadence switch, seat-blocked downgrade, confirm with busy state, cancellation with acknowledgement gate and resume, payment validation including expired-card detection, empty invoices, load error with retry and failNext failure simulation for three operations. However condition-b/evidence/capture-report.json activates only 2 of 12 captures (both default), and every non-default screenshot (condition-b/evidence/screenshots/1280x900-error.png, 1280x900-empty.png, 1280x900-success.png, 1280x900-restricted.png and the 390x844 equivalents) renders the loading skeleton, so no state beyond loading/default is visually verified.
rationale.accessibility_responsiveness: condition-b/evidence/checks.json reports axe violations [] with 31 passes and 1 incomplete, controls_without_accessible_name 0, no horizontal overflow at 1280 or 390 and no console/page errors; condition-b/project/styles.css provides a skip link, :focus-visible, aria-busy skeletons, aria-pressed segmented controls, prefers-reduced-motion, a wrapping sticky nav and invoice rows stacked at 600px. Scored 3 because condition-b/evidence/quality-gates.json is ok:false (accessible-names on demo-error, demo-empty, demo-fail and cancel-ack, whose #cancel-ack-label is empty in the static DOM).
rationale.implementation_quality: condition-b/project/app.js is organized into pure render functions with an IntersectionObserver scroll spy, consistent busy-state buttons, local-only validation (including expiry checks) and a failNext path that preserves prior state on failure; condition-b/evidence/checks.json shows no console or page errors. Scored 3 because condition-b/evidence/quality-gates.json is ok:false, and confirm operations are not aborted when the dialog is dismissed mid-flight - backdrop/Escape close does not cancel the pending setTimeout in the changeConfirm/cancelConfirm listeners, so a plan change or cancellation can still apply after the user closes the review.

critical_defects: condition-b/evidence/capture-report.json activates only 2 of 12 captures (both default); loading, empty, error, success and restricted were not activated, and their screenshots at both viewports (condition-b/evidence/screenshots/1280x900-error.png, 1280x900-empty.png, 1280x900-success.png, 1280x900-restricted.png, 390x844-error.png, 390x844-empty.png, 390x844-success.png, 390x844-restricted.png) all show the loading skeleton, so error, empty, success and restricted are unverified.

condition-b/evidence/quality-gates.json is ok:false - the accessible-names gate fails on demo-error, demo-empty, demo-fail and cancel-ack; #cancel-ack-label is empty in the static DOM (condition-b/project/index.html) until JavaScript fills it on dialog open.

Default state captures condition-b/evidence/screenshots/1280x900-default.png and 390x844-default.png show the loading skeleton rather than the default layout; ready-state evidence exists only in desktop.png and mobile.png.

condition-b/project/analysis.md reports 'a scripted browser pass covering 21 checks' and keyboard-verification results for the cancellation dialog, but the packet contains no test-output artifact to support them - condition-b/evidence/checks.json covers only rendered structure and axe.

Mid-flight dialog dismissal does not abort a pending confirmation: in condition-b/project/app.js the backdrop/Escape close handler does not cancel the pending setTimeout in els.changeConfirm or els.cancelConfirm, so state changes can complete after the user closes the review.
strengths: Cleanest default presentation in the pair: condition-b/evidence/screenshots/desktop.png and mobile.png show plan, price, next payment and seat usage above the fold, a section nav with a danger-coloured Cancel entry, and no overlay covering content.

Cancellation sits in its own danger section with a consequence list, acknowledgement gate, a destructive button disabled until acknowledged, and 'Keep my plan' as the visually primary exit (condition-b/project/index.html, condition-b/project/app.js openCancel).

Every consequential action has a designed failure path simulated via failNext that preserves the prior state and explains that nothing changed (condition-b/project/app.js applyChange, scheduleCancellation, payment submit).
axe reports zero violations (31 passes) with no horizontal overflow at either viewport and no console or page errors (condition-b/evidence/checks.json).

The member view removes owner-only controls and replaces them with plain-language notes rather than showing clickable-then-denied controls (condition-b/project/app.js renderBillingSection, renderDangerSection, renderPlanCard).

Mobile preserves the task order with a sticky wrapping nav, stacked plan cards, stacked invoice records and full-width dialog buttons (condition-b/project/styles.css, condition-b/evidence/screenshots/mobile.png).

verdict: Candidate A and Candidate B both deliver complete analyses and working prototypes, and both total 24 of 28 unweighted points (Candidate A: 4/4/4/3/3/3/3; Candidate B: 4/4/4/4/2/3/3 across product_understanding, ux_reasoning, design_judgment, visual_hierarchy, interaction_completeness, accessibility_responsiveness, implementation_quality; no weighting scheme was supplied). The pair separates on evidence versus presentation: Candidate A renders two non-default states at both viewports (loading, error, 8 of 12 captures activated), guards dialogs against mid-flight dismissal, but its default captures show a skeleton and its fixed prototype panel overlaps card headers; Candidate B verifies no state beyond the loading skeleton (2 of 12 captures activated) yet shows the cleaner, unobstructed default layout and the richer failure-path simulation. Prefer Candidate A where interaction-state proof and cancellation robustness matter most; prefer Candidate B where default-screen visual quality and failure handling breadth are weighted most. Neither candidate dominates on all seven dimensions.
limitations: This is one blinded judge pass over static artifacts, not a statistical test and not evidence of causation: state screenshots whose activation failed were scored as missing evidence rather than missing functionality; self-reported verification claims in both analysis.md files (Candidate A's rendered-state inspection, Candidate B's 21-check scripted pass) could not be corroborated by any artifact in the packet; the accessible-names failures in quality-gates.json conflict with the zero-unlabeled-control counts in checks.json for both candidates; no weighting scheme was provided so totals are simple sums; and this pass does not and cannot say which condition used which tooling, nor anything about real-user outcomes.
